title: Through the sea (Exodus 14)
hookLine: the waters part and they walk through on dry ground

cards: They're out. Israel walks out of Egypt with their dough still unrisen. And soon Pharaoh changes his mind again.

What have we done, letting our labor go? He takes six hundred chosen chariots and every other chariot in Egypt and rides after them. The Israelites, camped by the sea, look up and see dust on the horizon.
Water in front. Army behind. Nowhere to go.
And they turn on Moses: weren't there enough graves in Egypt, that you brought us out here to die?

teach.b: First, Moses's answer. Don't be afraid. Stand still and see what God will do.
The Lord will fight for you; you only have to keep quiet. Good advice, it sounds like. But then God says something surprising to Moses: why are you crying to me?
"Speak to the children of Israel to go forward." Standing still was a start, not the end. Second, the night.
The pillar of cloud that went ahead of them moves behind them, between Israel and Egypt, dark on one side and light on the other.

teach.h: A WIND ALL NIGHT, WALLS OF WATER.
teach.b: Moses stretches his hand over the sea, and a strong east wind blows all night and turns the sea into dry land. The waters are divided, a wall on their right and on their left, and they walk through.
Jewish tradition tells a story about this moment, a story people tell, not one in the text: the sea didn't part until one man, Nahshon, walked in up to his neck. Third, the morning.
The Egyptians follow, their chariot wheels clog, the waters come back.
At dawn Israel sees the shore, and the text says the people feared the Lord, and believed. Fourth, what Catholics hear.

teach.h: BAPTIZED IN THE CLOUD AND THE SEA.
teach.b: Paul writes that the Israelites were all baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea. That's why, at the Easter Vigil, this is the Old Testament reading the Roman Missal says may never be left out.
And when a priest blesses baptismal water, the prayer remembers the children of Abraham led dry-shod through the sea, a picture of everyone who will pass through the water of baptism.

how: At the Easter Vigil, the reading of Israel's crossing of the sea in Exodus 14 is never omitted, and the Church's blessing of baptismal water recalls the people led dry-shod through the sea.

s: God's last word before the crossing was stand still
Moses says stand still. then God says: speak to the children of Israel to go forward.
the Easter Vigil reading of the sea crossing may never be skipped
the other Old Testament readings can be shortened; Exodus 14 stays.
the Hebrew calls it the Red Sea
the Hebrew says yam suf, sea of reeds. Red Sea comes from the ancient Greek translation.

games.q: you're an Israelite at the edge of the sea. Pharaoh's chariots are coming. Moses has told you to stand still and see. what does God say next?
o: wait here until I fight for you.
go back and make peace with Pharaoh.
speak to the people: go forward.
games.why: go forward. the stillness was only the first step; the crossing comes from walking into the sea on dry ground.

practice: Name one place where you're standing at the water's edge: a test result you haven't opened, a form you haven't filled out, a door you haven't knocked on.
Be still with it first, that's allowed, then picture only the very first step, not the whole crossing, one foot onto the wet sand.
If you pray, listen for God's words to Moses, go forward; if you don't, just picture your foot moving.

wordCard.voice: Nahshon. The man Jewish tradition says walked into the sea up to his neck before the waters finally parted for Israel to cross on dry ground. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: the sea of reeds. the Greek translation made it the Red Sea, and the name stuck.

carryVoice: Your line: go forward. Stillness first, and then the step. Day three hundred seventy-three, done.

sources.q: Speak to the children of Israel to go forward.
